question: Ramu can do a work in 36 days and Kanu in 32 days. If they work on it together for 12 days, then what fraction of work is left?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Work done by Ramu in 12 days = 12 ÷ 36 = 1/3

Work done by Kanu in 12 days = 12 ÷ 32 = 3/8

Total work done together in 12 days = 1/3 + 3/8 = (8 + 9) / 24 = 17/24

Fraction of work left = 1 − 17/24 = 7/24

**∴ The correct answer is 7/24.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Time taken by Ramu to complete the work = 36 days

Time taken by Kanu to complete the work = 32 days

Number of days they worked together = 12 days

 
 

 **Person**
 **Days**
 **Total Work**
 **Efficiency**
 
 

 Ramu
 36
 288
 8
 
 

 Kanu
 32
 9
 
 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Total combined efficiency of Ramu and Kanu = 8 + 9 = 17 units/day

⇒ Total work done by both in 12 days = 17 × 12 = 204 units

⇒ Remaining work to be done = Total Work − Work Done = 288 − 204 = 84 units

⇒ Fraction of work left = Remaining Work ÷ Total Work

⇒ Fraction of work left = 84 ÷ 288 = 7/24

**∴ The correct answer is 7/24.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Pipes and Cisterns

This topic follows the same logic as Time and Work, where inlet pipes fill a tank (positive work) and outlet pipes empty it (negative work).

Work and Wages

Wages are always distributed in the exact ratio of the work done by each individual. If they work for an equal number of days, wages are distributed directly in the ratio of their efficiencies.

Alternate Day Work

When two people work on alternate days, combine their individual day works to find the total work completed in a 2-day cycle before progressing to the remaining amount.
